    AI Overview
    Wild: From Lost to Found on the Pacific Crest Trail is a 2012 memoir by Cheryl Strayed, chronicling her impulsive 1,100-mile solo hike to recover from her mother's death, drug addiction, and divorce. The 2014 film adaptation, directed by Jean-Marc Vallée, stars Reese Witherspoon (nominated for Best Actress) as Strayed and Laura Dern as her mother. 
    Watch the official trailer for the film adaptation of the memoir:
    44s
    Rotten Tomatoes Trailers
    YouTube• Jul 11, 2014
    Story Behind the Book and Movie 
    • The Journey: Following the death of her mother, the breakdown of her marriage, and a period of reckless behavior, Cheryl Strayed decided to hike the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) from California to Washington in 1995 with no prior hiking experience
      .
    • The Purpose: The hike was a journey of self-healing, intended to help her confront her grief and rebuild her life.
    • The Book: The memoir, Wild, was published in 2012 and became a number-one New York Times bestseller and an Oprah's Book Club selection.
    • The Movie: Released in 2014, the film was adapted by Nick Hornby and praised for its raw, emotional portrayal of survival and self-discovery. 
    Plot of the Book/Movie 
    • The Struggle: Strayed, played by Witherspoon in the film, battles immense physical pain, extreme weather, dangerous, heavily loaded gear ("Monster"), and haunting flashbacks of her past.
    • The Experience: Along the PCT, she faces moments of terror, loneliness, and, conversely, profound kindness from fellow hikers and strangers ("trail angels").
    • The Healing: The hike serves as a physical manifestation of her emotional journey, forcing her to confront her grief, addiction, and personal failures to emerge stronger, finding redemption and peace. 
    Key Cast Members (2014 Movie) 
    • Reese Witherspoon as Cheryl Strayed
    • Laura Dern as Bobbi Lambrecht (Cheryl's mother)
    • Thomas Sadoski as Paul (Cheryl's ex-husband) 
    The movie was a critical and commercial success, grossing $52.5 million and earning Oscar nominations for both Witherspoon and Dern.
